text:
maria-nd: Heads-up — we have multiple customers reporting 401 failures immediately after upgrading to py-sdk 1.43. Escalation from billing: retries caused duplicate charges for one account. :(

support-jen: ugh. Any repros or logs? customer says requests that worked on 1.42 now return 401 with signature error.

raj-sre: seeing same in our internal repro. stacktrace shows 'Invalid signature' from auth service. Interesting part: header name changed in SDK.

maria-nd: customer logs: 
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
x-rw-error: invalid_signature
x-rw-expected: sha256
x-rw-got: sha1
```
They were using HMAC-SHA1 before; 1.43 switched default signing to sha256 and also renamed header from `X-Redwood-Signature` -> `X-Redwood-Signature-V2` in the client. Server side still accepts legacy header but our load balancer auth rule only looks for exact header name in some regions (misses V2 header) so requests are unauthenticated and retried.

support-jen: can you paste minimal repro?

julian-eng: repro in 3 lines: 
```
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key=...)
resp = c.generate(...)
```
Upgrade to 1.43 => automatic signing uses v2 header. Quick curl showing failure: 
```
curl -v -H "X-Redwood-Signature-V2: sha256=abc" -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< x-rw-error: invalid_signature
```

raj-sre: workaround for support teams: pin to 1.42 while we triage: `pip install redwood-inference==1.42.0` or set fallback env var `REDWOOD_SIGNATURE_MODE=legacy` (we pushed this in a tiny patch to 1.43rc but it wasn't in the final).

maria-nd: which customers affected? list: AcmePayments, NovaDocs, and one enterprise pilot. Billing reported one doubled invoice from AcmePayments due to client retries after 401s.

support-jen: steps to reproduce and safe rollback added to the ticket. Do we have a mitigant server-side?

raj-sre: temp mitigant: auth layer config updated to accept both header names in region eu-west-1 and us-east-1. Need to push global rule but want to avoid flapping. I'll open a PR to extend header acceptance and add test coverage.

julian-eng: root cause summary: py-sdk 1.43 introduced a default signing format change (sha256 + header rename) to improve security. We forgot to coordinate the server-side header acceptance rollout and feature-flag the header rename. Also our client retries on 401s by default which led to duplicate billing for non-idempotent endpoints.

maria-nd: immediate customer communication: advise pin to 1.42 and/or set `REDWOOD_SIGNATURE_MODE=legacy`. Offer one-off billing credit for duplicated invoices and escalate to finance.

support-jen: posted guidance to status page and opened priority support cases. link to ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-4567 (internal).

raj-sre: triage checklist I ran: 
- reproduced with 1.43 on local env ✅
- confirmed 1.42 continues to work ✅
- confirmed header rename in SDK changelog ✅
- updated auth rules to accept `X-Redwood-Signature-V2` and `X-Redwood-Signature` in dev region ✅
- wrote e2e test to assert both headers accepted in auth proxy (PR #1289) ✅

julian-eng: planned next steps: backport env var fallback into a 1.43.1 patch release OR publish a 1.43.0 hotfix that respects legacy header by default and flips only when a new environment variable is set. I'll own the patch. ETA EOD.

maria-nd: can we also relax retry behavior for 401 on non-idempotent endpoints? we should avoid double charges.

raj-sre: yes, adding a retry policy change: do not retry on 4xx auth failures for write endpoints by default; opt-in for aggressive retries. Adding a config flag `RETRY_ON_401_FOR_WRITES=false`.

support-jen: customers updated, some pinned, one accepted our credit. Monitoring for further duplicates.

keeper-bot: deploy-bot: Rolling out auth-proxy rule update to staging -> success.

julian-eng: PR opened for 1.43.1: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1302 — patch reintroduces legacy header when `REDWOOD_SIGNATURE_MODE=legacy` or if `REDWOOD_LEGACY_HEADER=true`. Also changes default retry behavior for 401 on write endpoints.

maria-nd: thanks all. Please add a short postmortem once patch and server changes are live. We need release notes, a customer advisory, and a recommended pin in our docs.

support-jen: filed follow-up: create KB article with pinned command, env var, and billing contact. I'll link it here when ready. :thumbsup:

julian-eng: patch released 1.43.1 and server header acceptance rolled global. I'll add unit tests and a regression in our CI matrix to catch header renames in the future.

maria-nd: closing loop: confirm with AcmePayments that duplicates were credited; they replied yes. Good job team. :party_popper:
